title: Pol Roti
description: Soft coconut flatbread, perfect with lunu miris for breakfast.
steps: Mix flour, coconut, onion, chilli and salt in a bowl.
Add water little by little and knead into a soft dough.
Divide into balls and flatten each one on a banana leaf or oiled paper.
Cook on a hot pan for 3–4 minutes per side until golden spots appear.

title: Dhal Curry (Parippu)
description: Creamy red lentils cooked in coconut milk with turmeric and curry leaves.
steps: Cook the lentils with thin coconut milk, turmeric and half the onion until soft.
Add the thick coconut milk and salt, and simmer for 2 minutes.
In another pan, fry mustard seeds, the rest of the onion, garlic and curry leaves in oil.
Pour the tempering over the dhal and stir.

title: Chicken Kottu Roti
description: The famous street food: chopped godamba roti stir-fried with vegetables, egg and curry.
ingredients: 1 cup cooked chicken curry with gravy
steps: Fry the onion, then add carrot, leek and cabbage and cook for 3 minutes.
Push vegetables aside, scramble the eggs in the pan.
Add the roti strips and chicken with gravy.
Chop and mix everything with two metal spatulas until well combined. Season and serve hot.

title: Watalappan
description: A steamed coconut custard pudding with jaggery, cardamom and cashews.
steps: Melt the jaggery in the coconut milk over low heat, then let it cool.
Beat the eggs lightly and mix them with the jaggery milk and spices.
Strain into a bowl, decorate with cashews and cover with foil.
Steam for 45–50 minutes until set. Chill before serving.

title: Faluda
description: A sweet, colourful rose-syrup milk drink with basil seeds and ice cream.
ingredients: 2 tbsp basil seeds, soaked in water for 15 minutes
steps: Put rose syrup at the bottom of two tall glasses.
Add basil seeds and jelly.
Pour in the cold milk slowly.
Top with ice cream and serve immediately.

title: Egg Hoppers (Appa)
description: Bowl-shaped rice flour pancakes with crispy edges and a soft egg in the middle.
steps: Mix rice flour, yeast, sugar and warm water. Leave to ferment for 4–6 hours.
Stir in coconut milk and salt to make a thin batter.
Pour a ladle into a hot hopper pan and swirl it around the sides.
Crack an egg in the middle, cover and cook for 3–4 minutes.
